anomalies.observed: The VDD power pins of both the FCC (STM32H753VITx) and NAVC (STM32F405RGTx) are on single-node nets named unconnected-(...-VDD-...), meaning they are not connected to any supply rail.
anomalies.expected: All VDD pins must be connected to the 3.3V rail, as stated in the specification: '3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs'.

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: Both microcontrollers receive no core power and will not operate, rendering the entire board non-functional.

anomalies.observed: The netlist contains no CH330 USB-UART bridge components, despite the specification listing two such bridges in the Connections sheet.
anomalies.expected: Two CH330 USB-UART bridges should be present to provide the specified UART-to-USB programming/debug interfaces.

evidence.quote: The components list includes USB3, USB4, USB5, USB6, but no CH330 or similar USB-UART bridge IC.

anomalies.impact: The UART-to-USB programming and debug interfaces are missing, preventing communication with the board via USB UART.

anomalies.observed: The PCA9685PW PWM driver's address pin A0 (pin 1) is connected to the +3.3V rail.
anomalies.expected: A0 should be tied to GND to set the I2C address to 0x40, as specified: 'PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40'.

evidence.quote: PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: The PCA9685 will respond to I2C address 0x41 instead of 0x40, so the flight controller cannot control the PWM outputs at the expected address.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple severe anomalies. The most critical is that both MCUs have their VDD pins unconnected, so they will not power on. Additionally, the two CH330 USB-UART bridges specified are missing, and the PCA9685 PWM driver has its A0 address pin tied high, changing its I2C address from 0x40 to 0x41.
